actions.operation: Reduce the depth of the main cutout.

parameters.inferred_depth_direction: Toward the open end in CAD -Z
parameters.existing_overall_slot_depth: Approximately 40 mm from z=-150 mm to z=-110 mm
parameters.revised_overall_slot_depth: Approximately 30 mm from z=-150 mm to z=-120 mm

actions.target: The main cutout of the spanner.
actions.relational_constraint: The cutout must become 10 mm shallower relative to its existing depth.
actions.unresolved_reference: Resolved as the open-end engagement slot F011, not the shallow handle pocket F004. F004 is only 1 mm deep and does not define the functional spanner opening. The slot depth is controlled by root wall FACE 18 and root transitions FACE 17 and FACE 19.
steps: Localize the edit to section R03, the open-ended fork region, and feature F011, the open-end engagement slot. Do not modify F004, the shallow 1 mm handle pocket, because it is a cosmetic and mass-reduction recess rather than the functional spanner cutout.

Use the front broad side of the wrench, corresponding to the +Y semantic front view and the XZ sketch orientation, to inspect or reconstruct the through-slot profile. The slot passes through the complete wrench thickness from y=0 mm to y=15 mm.
Retain the two existing straight jaw boundaries at x=-10 mm and x=10 mm. These boundaries generate the functional contact faces FACE 20 and FACE 22 and must not move laterally.
Move the closed root of the slot 10 mm toward the open tips, which is the CAD -Z direction. Relocate the planar root represented by FACE 18 from z=-110 mm to z=-120 mm.

Translate the two radius-5 root transitions represented by FACE 17 and FACE 19 by the same 10 mm in CAD -Z. The revised transition extents should be approximately z=-125 mm to z=-120 mm, with tangency to the unchanged jaw walls at approximately z=-125 mm.

Maintain the existing root construction: a horizontal root segment from approximately x=-5 mm to x=5 mm at z=-120 mm, joined tangentially to the x=-10 mm and x=10 mm jaw walls by two 5 mm radius arcs.

If editable feature history exists, modify the sketch or profile that generated F011 and regenerate its through-all cut along Y. Constrain both jaw lines, the root line, both 5 mm arcs, symmetry about x=0, and all arc-to-line tangencies before rebuilding.

If the model is being edited as an imported solid, first create an additive repair sketch on an XZ-oriented plane covering the old slot-root region, approximately x=-10.1 mm to x=10.1 mm and z=-125.1 mm to z=-109.9 mm. Extrude and union this profile through the full y=0 mm to y=15 mm thickness to fill the old root and transition void.

After the additive repair, sketch the revised U-shaped slot with straight sides at x=-10 mm and x=10 mm, side-wall tangency ending near z=-125 mm, two 5 mm root arcs, and the new root line at z=-120 mm. Extend the sketch beyond the open tip at z=-150 mm so that the cut remains open-ended.
Cut the revised slot through all material along the Y direction. Confirm that the result remains one connected solid and that no residual faces from the previous root remain inside the slot.

Inspect the rebuilt root for tangent continuity between the straight jaw surfaces and the two radius-5 transitions. Verify that the material added behind the new root strengthens the fork-to-handle load path without changing the exterior fork profile F010.

actions.operation: Preserve the spanner size by maintaining the specified separation between the parallel surfaces.

parameters.required_relationship: Parallel, opposed, and separated by 20 mm

actions.target: The parallel surfaces defining the spanner size.
actions.relational_constraint: The surfaces must remain parallel and 20 mm apart after the cutout depth is reduced.
actions.unresolved_reference: Resolved as the opposed open-end jaw contact faces FACE 20 and FACE 22 in feature F011. Their planes are x=-10 mm and x=10 mm, respectively, giving the required 20 mm wrench size.
steps: Use FACE 20 and FACE 22 as the controlling functional interfaces for the wrench size. FACE 20 is the planar jaw contact surface at x=-10 mm, and FACE 22 is the opposed planar jaw contact surface at x=10 mm.
In the revised slot sketch, constrain the two jaw lines to be parallel to the CAD Z direction and apply a 20 mm perpendicular separation constraint between them.
Prefer a symmetric constraint about the longitudinal center plane x=0 so that the jaw faces remain at x=-10 mm and x=10 mm. Do not offset, taper, rotate, or widen either contact surface.

Allow only the longitudinal termination of the jaw surfaces to change as the root transitions move toward the opening. Their revised straight portions should run from the open tip near z=-150 mm to the new transition tangency near z=-125 mm.
Regenerate the cut and identify the replacement B-rep faces corresponding to the original FACE 20 and FACE 22, because face indices may change after the Boolean operation.
Measure the minimum normal distance between the regenerated planar jaw faces and verify a value of 20.000 mm within the modeling tolerance.
Check that the surface normals are opposed and that the angular deviation between the two planes is zero within tolerance. Confirm that the opening remains accessible from the minimum-Z end.
Verify in the +Y front view that the slot is visibly 10 mm shallower while its width is unchanged. Also confirm in the +X and -X side views that the cut remains through the full 15 mm thickness.
Do not alter the outer fork walls FACE 16 and FACE 23, the handle geometry, the box-end bore, or the shallow handle pocket.

intention: Reduce weakening of the tool caused by the excessively deep main cutout.
Retain the same functional spanner size while making the cutout shallower.
